answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring each identity to post a refundable stake that is slashed on proven misbehavior, so creating many fake agents multiplies the attacker's locked capital instead of multiplying their influence. Reputation then accrues slowly per identity, like an ember that must be tended before it glows, and decays without honest work, so a swarm of opal-bright new accounts cannot outvote established ones. A quartz-like audit trail of signed transactions lets peers verify that reputation was earned, not bought, making mass fakery expensive and slow.
